text:
Fiona Park: Heads-up from the auklet-int4 onboarding canary: we're seeing structured-output failures where the funcall payload is valid JSON but wrapped in an HTML 
 block (streaming only). Parsers treat it as garbage and the funcall stage aborts.
Gabe Holmes: Wait HTML? Can you paste a raw stream capture?
Fiona Park: Pasted snippet below. This was from a 2MB token trace where the final toolcall array comes through as an HTML chunk.
Fiona Park: ```

[{"tool":"search","args":{"q":"redwood inference"}},
 {"tool":"summarize","args":{"length":50}}]


```
Irma Soto: Hmm — model seems to emit helpful markup in some prompts (maybe from pretraining). Only happens when stream=true and batch<=2. Failure rate ~0.9% over 5k canary calls. Non-streamed mirrored run succeeded.
Nora Patel: Any token-level evidence? Might be decoding sampling that prefers literal HTML tokens.
Fiona Park: Attached token fragment: `[TOK_401]="<" [TOK_402]="pre" [TOK_403]=">\n["`. The `
` tokens are real output, not escape sequences.
Gabe Holmes: That explains it. Runtime streaming boundary + model emits markup as separate chunk. Parsers expect raw NDJSON/JSON per funcall and choke on leading/trailing tags.
Irma Soto: Quick mitigations: 1) Gatekeeper strip known wrappers (`
`, ``) before parse. 2) Runtime sanitizer that performs token-boundary-aware trimming for common wrappers when stream=true. 3) Onboarding tests: fuzz feed HTML tokens into stream splits to surface this earlier.
Nora Patel: I don't love automatic stripping by default since it could hide models spitting non-json noise. Can we make it opt-in per-canary and record a `wrapper_stripped` metric with reason labels (html_tag, markdown_codeblock, surrounding_text)?
Gabe Holmes: Agreed. Also add a new lint rule in onboarding: "no leading non-json tokens > 0.1%". Fail the canary if exceeded.
Fiona Park: Proposal: gatekeeper config `structured_output.sanitizers: ["strip_html_tags","strip_markdown_codeblock","require_leading_bracket"]` with `telemetry.sanitizer_tags=true`. Default: none.
Irma Soto: Implementation note: `strip_html_tags` should only remove matching open/close tags at the very start/end of the payload to avoid removing legitimate strings containing `<` characters. Also record the original raw bytes in a short-lived debug buffer for audit.
Gabe Holmes: I'll prototype a minimal sanitizer in gatekeeper (PR). Nora, can you add the onboarding lint and a fuzz test that injects `
`, triple backticks, and random alpha tokens at chunk boundaries?
Nora Patel: Yep, will add a harness job that varies chunk sizes 1..6 and injects wrappers with probability p=0.01..0.5. Dashboard will show wrapper_hit_rate and post-sanitizer parse_success_rate.
Fiona Park: Action items: 
- Fiona: attach full token traces and example requests to the repro issue (done today)
- Gabe: gatekeeper sanitizer PR (taking)
- Nora: onboarding lint + fuzz harness + dashboard slice
- Irma: update onboarding checklist & write short doc on sanitizer semantics
Fiona Park: One question: do we block auklet-int4 onboarding until sanitizer is in place? Current plan: hold for production rollout; allow canary in staging with sanitizer opt-in only and telemetry on. If wrapper_hit_rate > 0.3% or post-sanitizer parse failure > 0.2% we stop.
Gabe Holmes: fine to proceed with staging opt-in. We'll gate the change behind a feature flag and add a logline for each sanitized payload.
jenkins-bot: [automated] canary-run recorded 1825004321: 5000 requests, wrapper_hit_rate=0.009, parse_fail_rate_before_sanitize=0.009, parse_fail_rate_after_sanitize=0.0007.
Irma Soto: Interesting — sanitizer drops failures from 0.9% to 0.07% on that run. Need follow-up to ensure sanitizer doesn't change semantics in edge cases.
Nora Patel: I'll include a golden-set regression check comparing outputs pre/post sanitize on a sample of 1000 requests.
Fiona Park: OK. If golden-set diffs are small (<0.1% functional change), we can accept sanitizer for staging. Otherwise we iterate.
Gabe Holmes: Sounds good. I'll open the PR and link the tests. Ping me for review.
Irma Soto: Thanks everyone.
Nora Patel: Thanks :rocket:
